title: Pivotality of an affine threshold
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, and suppose that $f(x)$ is the sign of $a_0+\sum_{k=1}^n a_k x_k$ for every $x$, where the sign is $+1$ for a nonnegative argument and $-1$ otherwise. For a coordinate $i$ and input $x$, write $R_i(x)=a_0+\sum_{k\ne i}a_kx_k$. Then $f$ is pivotal at $x$ in coordinate $i$ if and only if $-|a_i|\le R_i(x)<|a_i|$.
hypotheses_covered: Boolean function f on the n-dimensional sign cube
Real intercept a₀ and real coefficients a
f is represented everywhere by the stated threshold of its affine linear form
Input x in the n-dimensional sign cube
